Pasco County couple finally receives $24k tax refund after months of frustration TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — A Pasco County couple has finally received a $24,851 income tax refund they had been waiting for since February after months of delays and frustration with the IRS.
 Cathy Boucher and her husband say they received the runaround from the IRS and struggled to get answers about their refund. After eight months of uncertainty, they contacted Better Call Behnken.
 [sailthru_widget name="Sailthru Widget Block" sailthru_list="8 on Your Side" title="8 on Your Side"]
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Thank you for your help. The nightmare is over," Boucher said.
 Boucher said the couple filed their taxes in mid-February and were asked to verify their identities in March. They were initially told it would take nine weeks to receive their refund.
 Later, they were told to expect a 180-day wait, but the money still did not arrive.

 "After eight months plus of uncertainty and worry and concern, after you talked to us and worked your magic, we were assigned an advocate with the IRS," Boucher said.
 Boucher said she had applied for a taxpayer advocate the previous month. Although she received a case number, she was told the process could mean another 90-day wait.
 Advertisement Advertisement That is when she decided to contact Consumer Investigator Shannon Behnken to help escalate the issue.
 After calls from Behnken, the IRS contacted Boucher and assigned the couple an advocate. Weeks later, they finally received their refund.
 "We're just so happy and wish we had called you sooner," Boucher said.
 Boucher said the money arrived just in time. The couple plans to use part of the refund to purchase Christmas presents for children in need.
 Boucher said they have always enjoyed receiving tax refunds but never expected this one to be so large.
 The experience also taught the couple a lesson about withholding taxes.
 Advertisement Advertisement "We don't over withhold on anything. We still hope to receive a refund, but it'd be better to be closer to what we owe than to have any kind of a refund," Boucher said. "So that's the lesson to learn, not over withhold because it's not worth the risk."
